lead: After 20 wk amniotic fluid is mostly fetal urine, removed by fetal swallowing; it peaks at about 900 mL at 34–36 wk. AFI adds the deepest pool of four quadrants (normal about 9–25 cm); DVP is the single deepest pool.
f: AFI over 25 cm or DVP over 8 cm · Chronic (common, gradual) or acute (rare, under 20 wk, usually monozygotic twins) · Causes: idiopathic (commonest), diabetes (fetal polyuria), GI atresia (oesophageal, duodenal), anencephaly, myotonic dystrophy, twins and TTTS, hydrops

sc: Polyhydramnios; newborn drools and chokes, NG tube coils → Oesophageal atresia with TOF
Polyhydramnios with a double bubble → Duodenal atresia (Down syndrome)

f: Uterus large for dates, tense; fetal parts and heart hard to find; fluid thrill · Discomfort, breathlessness · Unstable lie · Detailed scan, OGTT, TORCH, syphilis, blood group and antibodies, karyotype if anomaly

Preterm labour, malpresentation · At ROM: cord prolapse and abruption · PPH (atony) · Treat the cause (glucose control, laser for TTTS) · Severe and symptomatic (AFI over 40): slow amnioreduction · Indomethacin 25 mg 6-hourly under 32 wk for no more than 72 h (ductus closure) · Labour: check the lie, controlled ARM, oxytocin ready for PPH

sc: Polyhydramnios: membranes rupture, sudden pain, dark bleed → Abruption

f: AFI under 5 cm or DVP under 2 cm (5–8 borderline); anhydramnios = no pool · Fluid leaks out: ROM (commonest) · Less urine: FGR, placental insufficiency, post-term, renal agenesis (Potter) · Urine blocked: posterior urethral valves in boys · Drugs: NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, ARBs · Mnemonic DRIPP: Demise, Renal, IUGR, Post-term, PROM

sc: Boy, large bladder, keyhole sign → Posterior urethral valves
42 wk, liquor low, CTG normal → Post-term: induce

f: Watery leak, reduced movements · Uterus small for dates, fetal parts easily felt, often breech · Sterile speculum (pool), FBC, CRP, HVS if ROM · Scan: AFI, growth, kidneys, bladder; UA Doppler if growth is poor

From the cause: chorioamnionitis, preterm birth, stillbirth · From low volume: pulmonary hypoplasia (before about 22 wk), limb contractures, talipes, Potter facies, cord compression · ROM at or after 34–36 wk: induce · ROM before 34–36 wk: erythromycin 250 mg 6-hourly × 10 days, dexamethasone if under 34 wk, watch for infection · FGR: timing by Doppler and CTG · Renal anomaly: fetal medicine

sc: Breech at 37 wk, AFI 3 cm → ECV is usually not offered
Newborn with flat nose, low-set ears, talipes, respiratory failure → Potter sequence (renal agenesis)
tr: ACE inhibitors are banned in pregnancy: fetal renal failure, oligohydramnios, hypocalvaria
